description: Governance across the enterprise at a glance: dozens of agents on several foundries, all under one layer. The briefing surfaces what needs review, what is on track, and what the knowledge graph caught.
Field-level routing provenance. Every customer-sensitive element resolved in the in-environment SLM; the frontier model ran one reasoning task on non-PII inputs only. Zero PII or PCI to the frontier.

Classification by meaning, not keyword. The knowledge graph classifies a customer's renewal price as customer-specific PII under DG-04 — the real governance-stack tool (Neo4j) re-rendered in the platform.

Three gates govern every task: is it safe to send (no PII or PCI), is it worth sending (the task genuinely needs the frontier model), and is it within budget. A task must pass all three; everything else stays local.
Per-task routing and cost together. The frontier model handled 3 of 24 tasks, all complex and all on non-PII inputs; routing saved 71% against the all-frontier counterfactual.
One governance model across every AI initiative and foundry — customer care, Bluehost customer AI, and engineering copilots. Every agent action is explainable against the policy that governed it.
